findings.reason: The Brief preserves latency reduction with retrieval-quality preservation, the evidence-grounded report, all mandatory reference constraints, and both exclusions. It invents no method or percentage and promotes no preference.

The single_gpu constraint matches the policy, is explicitly attributed as a system default, and is scoped to scientific execution. Its assumption identifies the authority and affected field without claiming hardware availability. No unsupported default is introduced.

All seven mandatory requirements are covered by acceptance expectations and evidence obligations. Both targets link to their requirements; the report deliverable covers the objective and constraints. Evidence obligations require supported claims, disclosure of missing measurements, and a compliance account.

The Brief provides an actionable investigation goal, a bound reference input, explicit execution constraints, a report deliverable, and usable acceptance and evidence expectations. Unchosen methods and numeric thresholds do not block this qualitative research task.

limitations: No empirical measurements are supplied; compilation acceptance does not establish latency improvement or retrieval-quality preservation.
Experimental methods and numeric thresholds remain unchosen.
The policy-default hardware profile does not establish hardware availability.
